text:
Anna K: Quick sync — after Friday's launch we've got a growing long tail of signals. Need to decide what the next 2 sprints look like: prioritise customer-facing bug fixes, or push a couple of small enhancements that unblock adoption?

Mike L: +1 to triage first. Can we run an impact x frequency matrix? quick idea: P0/P1 = customer-facing regressions or crashes, P2 = annoying but workarounds, P3 = nice-to-have.

Samir: From infra telemetry, error spikes are concentrated in the streaming path for sessions > 8k tokens. That's hitting 3 paying customers (CUST-112, CUST-118). Might be regressions from last kernel change.

Julia P: Customers flagged CUST-112 for SLA breach — SRE escalated earlier. I'd treat that as showstopper (P0). The rest of the smaller UX asks could wait.

Ben_Ops: +1 on order: P0 fixes, then high-ROI enhancements. Also note dedicated customers want a patch rather than a full release (they prefer hotfix branch).

Anna K: Proposal: sprint A (2 weeks): ship emergency patch for streaming regression + 2 P1 bugfixes that unblock onboarding. Sprint B: 2-week slot for 2 small enhancements that directly move trial->paid conversion (promo UX tweaks + faster onboarding flow).

Mike L: Sounds reasonable. Need owners and acceptance criteria. For the patch: Samir to lead, Ben to coordinate hotfix branch and deploy plan, Julia for QA acceptance with CUST-112.

Samir: I can own the patch. Quick plan: revert kernel heuristic change on hotfix branch, add additional telemetry, and run a targeted canary against CUST-112. ETA: 3 working days to a hotfix candidate.

Julia P: QA acceptance criteria: no reproduce of the streaming OOM on 10k token replay, full integration test passing, and verified with CUST-112 staging. I'll sign off once those pass.

Anna K: For the P1s, suggest: 1) onboarding API error sanitization (reduces trial friction), 2) docs snippet for rerouting on throttles (low-effort). Owners: Mike for API fix, Julia for docs. Can we estimate effort?

Mike L: API fix looks like 2 dev days + 1 review. I'll slot it into sprint A after patch candidate stabilises.

Ben_Ops: Docs snippet is trivial — ops can draft and ship same-day. Also I'll prepare a hotfix rollout checklist: tagging, changelog, runtime config toggles, rollback step.

Anna K: Sprint B enhancements — we should pick the ones with measurable CVR impact. Ideas: inline trial-to-paid CTA on SDK examples, and a 'quickstart' template for common infra. Both look 3 dev days each.

Samir: Make sure we include perf targets for the quickstart; if it degrades cold-start p99 we need to adjust.

Mike L: Agree. Can we set a guardrail: any enhancement that risks >5% p99 regression gets delayed.

Julia P: Scheduling note — we need a short postmortem doc for the streaming regression root cause and action items, even if we hotfix. I'll create a page and link it in the ticket.

Anna K: Action items: Samir creates CUST-112 hotfix PR and links tests (due EOD +3 days). Ben drafts rollout checklist (due EOD +2 days). Mike scopes API P1 (EOD +2). Julia drafts PM/QA acceptance and starts PM doc (EOD +4). I'll consolidate into the sprint A board and run a sync Friday 10am.

Ben_Ops: deploy-bot: recent deploy 1767012200 to prod by @deploy-bot — no rollback events.

Samir: A note — if the hotfix requires kernel rework, we should coordinate with eng-runtime to avoid wider perf regressions. I'll loop in that team if we go that route.

Mike L: OK. If anything slips, fallback is to prioritize P0 only and move P1s to the next micro-sprint.

Anna K: Thanks all. I'll create the sprint ticket bundles and assign owners. Friday sync 10am — calendar invite incoming. :thumbsup:
